explanation: A mixture. It fires on a word-piece right after a prefix in technical or scientific compounds: 'intr' + ac/al ('intracranial', 'intralobar'), 'gal' + actic, 'Raster' + ize, Milky + ' Way'. It also fires on statistics words that follow another word, like 'confidence interval', 'pooled sensitivity', 'sensitivity analysis' and 'background noise'. There are scattered weaker hits in math and code text.

Fires on the first sub-word piece of a rare or foreign proper noun or technical word, right after a word boundary, where the rest of the word is still to come (' W'+istar, ' mam'+mary, ' Cor'+vallis, ' Cam'+bridgeshire, ' tro'+phic, Ha+'em'+agogus). Whole common words and the final pieces of a word stay weak.

Fires on a middle sub-word piece inside a multi-token word that is rare, foreign or a proper name (Turkish 'h[uk]uk', 'H[ual]ong', 'St[ur]ridge', 'r[hes]us', 'ch[ym]otrypsin', 'npl[ur]als'), including pieces of CJK characters. It is weak on ordinary English words and code keywords.

A mixture. It fires on word-pieces inside biomedical or rare words (hy[g]roma, spermato[zo]a, def[orestation], ped[ag]ogy, Sy[g]ic). It also fires on 'except' in the licence line 'you may not use this file except', on 'and' joining paired harms ('pests and diseases', 'moisture loss and decay', 'reproductive and respiratory'), and on prevention verbs ('prevent', 'ensure', 'defies').

Fires on function or connector tokens inside fixed boilerplate formulas whose next token is highly predictable: 'this == o' in equals(), 'Sent from my', 'subject to the Mozilla', 'On order of the Court', DOI dots, '// +build', 'Post navigation', 'Keep shopping', 'S.W.2d'. It is driven by the surrounding template context more than by the token itself.

A mixture, mostly tied to Chinese or East Asian context and to code or markup. It fires on CJK characters, on Aliyun SDK identifiers, on markup tokens like ' <' or ' </' in nested XML/WXML, on punctuation in code, and on digits in postal codes, ISBNs and registration numbers. It also fires on 'or' in the GPL line 'version 2 of the License, or'.

A broad mixture. Its strongest consistent hit is ' express' in the licence phrase 'either express or implied'. It also fires on LaTeX backslashes in math, on content words after a subject or relative clause ('who received', 'his loving wife', 'cover around', 'who live'), and on units and code fragments. No single shared rule.

Fires inside institutional or proper-noun names, especially in German, Romance and Danish text: 'of' in 'College of Medicine', 'Ministry of', 'Professor of'; pieces of German compounds (Land+esvorsitz, Anschl+uss, Jahres+rück); nationality and place words ('Royal Australian', 'Greenock', 'Sudan'). Non-English running text seems to boost it in general.

Fires on tokens in formal header or boilerplate address lines: the street number after 'Inc., ' in the FSF address, the ')' after 'Reuters' in a datelined byline, the '.\n\n' ending the BSD licence sentence, and commas or periods after company names in legal captions ('Inc.,', 'Association,'). There are also scattered hits in ordinary text.

A mixture. It fires on ' do' after 'defmodule Name' in Elixir, on pandas tokens (' Frame' in DataFrame, ' pd'), on TV call letters '(WXYZ)', on a CJK surname in a name list, and on middle pieces of foreign names and words (Irigoyen, Jabal, Giovanni).

Fires on words about religion, spirituality, mythology, psychology or the mind ('mythology', 'Paganism'/'modern', 'secular', 'soul', 'devotional', 'psych'-, 'Hypnotherapy', 'knowledge' after 'Seek'). It also fires more weakly on pieces of psychoactive drug names (clonidine, scopolamine, antipsychotic).

Fires on equality or existence test operators and names in code: '==', '===', '!=', 'EQUAL'/'equal'/'assert_equals', 'isset', 'is_null', 'defined', 'IfEmpty', 'NOT EXISTS'. It also fires on 'not present' and 'not found' in conditional comments. It is strongest when the token is the comparison inside an if or assert.

A mixture. It fires most strongly on '0' inside long runs of zeros. It also fires on the closing ' License' in 'limitations under the License', on '.net' in jsfiddle URLs, on '.Text' or '.New' after a namespace, on the 'opor' piece in osteoporosis, on '1' in an exponent '^{-1}', and on surnames after first names.

No clear pattern. It fires on '*var' tokens in generated algebra problems ('*k', '*g', '*p'), on '.net' in jsfiddle, on surname suffixes in legal lists of names (Jernigan, Murchison, Dahlin), on digits in years, and on assorted verbs and function words in news text.
